newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe threatens to arrest telecoms businessman.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe threatens to arrest telecoms businessman.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government has threatened to arrest a businessman who has been battling in the courts for three years for a licence to operate a cellular phone network, a local newspaper reported on Thursday.

The weekly independent Financial Gazette quoted Information, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Joyce Mujuru as saying Strive Masiyiwa of Econet had unlawfully installed leased telecommunications equipment and tested it.
Mujuru and Masiyiwa were unavailable for comment.
"It's illegal under the security and defence laws of this country for one to put up and operate telecommunications systems without a licence or lawful authority," Mujuru was quoted as saying.
"He might be arrested and jailed because its illegal and the laws of the land don't allow that. He must know that telecommunications is a very sensitive area," she said.
Mujuru ordered Masiyiwa to sell his Z$100 million (U.S.$8.9 million) cellular equipment to his main Econet rival or risk government confiscation.
"We have decided as government that they have to sell the equipment to the winning group (tenderer) or the government will confiscate the equipment," she was quoted as saying.

Masiyiwa told the newspaper he would challenge that order in court and was appealing also against a March 7 government decision to award a tender to operate the private cellular phone network to Telecel, a consortium of local businesses and a foreign firm.
Controversy has been raging around the government decision to give the licence to a company in which President Robert Mugabe's nephew Leo Mugabe is a partner.
